original.scoring_instruction: After every sentence, assess how likely an average human reader would be to think that sentence was AI-generated. Use an integer from 0 to 100, where 0 means very human-like and 100 means obviously AI-generated. Put the sentence's normal closing punctuation first, then immediately append the assessment as <AI SCORE: n>.

paraphrase.description: Semantic paraphrase; same direction and range.
paraphrase.scoring_instruction: After each sentence, predict the chance that a typical human reader would flag that sentence as sounding AI-written rather than naturally human-written. Give an integer percentage from 0 to 100, where 0 means completely human-written and 100 means unmistakably AI-written. Put the sentence's normal closing punctuation first, then immediately append the prediction as <AI SCORE: n>.

reverse.scoring_instruction: After every sentence, estimate the probability that a typical human reader would judge that sentence as naturally human-written rather than AI-written. Use an integer from 0 to 100, where 0 means unmistakably AI-written and 100 means completely naturally human-written. Put the sentence's normal closing punctuation first, then immediately append the assessment as <HUMAN SCORE: n>.

minimal.description: Same AI-likeness semantics with minimal numeric tag.
minimal.scoring_instruction: After every sentence, assess how likely an average human reader would be to think that sentence was AI-generated. Use an integer from 0 to 100, where 0 means very human-like and 100 means obviously AI-generated. Put the sentence's normal closing punctuation first, then immediately append only the score in square brackets, for example [37].

primary_robustness_claims: GPT-5.5 has greater within-output Live-to-Post rank stability than Gemini in the same direction across elicitation variants.
Gemini has a larger normalized Post-minus-Live shift than GPT-5.5 in the same direction across elicitation variants.
On the fixed Replay subset, Gemini's Post-minus-Replay component remains larger than its Replay-minus-Live component across elicitation variants.

questions.task: Write 6-8 sentences as a first-person social-media update about unexpectedly spending a rainy Saturday reorganizing a storage room with an old friend. Mention finding a concert ticket from 2009, arguing briefly about whether to throw away a broken lamp, ordering noodles halfway through, and ending with the fact that the room still is not completely finished. Keep it ordinary and conversational, not inspirational.

Write 6-8 sentences as an informal message to a parents' WhatsApp group. The class picnic has moved from Friday to Sunday because of weather, the meeting point is unchanged, families should bring water but not food because lunch is provided, and one parent has already volunteered to bring spare hats. Mention that your own child is disappointed about Friday but excited about Sunday. Do not make the message sound official.

Write 6-8 sentences as a casual first-person workplace anecdote about a product demo that nearly failed because a conference-room adapter was missing. A colleague found one in another room, the customer waited about seven minutes, the demo eventually worked, and the customer laughed about having the same problem the week before. Keep it suitable for a personal LinkedIn post but avoid lessons, leadership slogans, or a motivational ending.

Write 6-8 sentences as a first-person neighborhood post about a tiny free-book shelf that appeared beside a bus stop. Mention seeing a cookbook, two children's books, and an old detective novel there; a teenager took the detective novel; someone had left a handwritten note asking people not to leave magazines in the rain. Keep the observation low-key and specific.

Write 6-8 sentences as a first-person account of using a robot vacuum for three months. It handles dust well, gets stuck under one particular chair, once dragged a phone cable across the room, and is useful enough that you still run it most weekdays. You bought it yourself. Include one concrete annoyance and one concrete benefit, and do not make it sound like advertising.

Write 6-8 sentences as a first-person social post about a frustrating grocery delivery. The delivery window was 18:00-20:00, it arrived at 21:15, two refrigerated items were warm, customer support refunded those two items, and the driver was polite. Tell it as a specific story rather than a formal complaint and avoid exaggerating what happened.

Write 6-8 sentences as an informal message to close friends about changing Saturday dinner plans. The original restaurant cannot seat the group before 22:00, you found a smaller place at 19:30, it is about ten minutes farther away, and one friend has already said either option is fine. Ask the group what they prefer without turning the message into a poll or a formal invitation.

Write 6-8 sentences as a first-person recommendation after using a local bicycle-repair shop. They replaced a worn chain the same day, called before adding a new brake cable, charged slightly less than the initial estimate, and the shop itself is cramped and easy to miss. Explain why you would go back while keeping both the positive and inconvenient details.

Write 6-8 sentences as a first-person travel anecdote about arriving at a small coastal town with two tired children just before dinner. The hotel room was not ready for another twenty minutes, the receptionist gave the children paper and pencils, you walked to a bakery next door, and by the time you returned the room was ready. Focus on the small episode, not on reviewing the whole trip.

Write 6-8 sentences as a first-person post about missing a train by less than a minute during a weekend trip. The next train was 42 minutes later, a station cafe was still open, you had no urgent connection afterward, and a stranger at the next table recommended a walking route you later used. Keep the tone mildly amused rather than dramatic.

Write 6-8 sentences as a first-person post about changing your mind about grocery self-checkout. You used to avoid it, recently found it convenient for a basket of six items, still dislike it when buying produce that must be searched manually, and had an employee help when one barcode failed. Ground the opinion only in this experience and do not generalize about automation or jobs.

Write 6-8 sentences as a first-person recommendation to friends about a small cafe near a museum. The coffee was good, service was slow because only one person was working, the outdoor tables were quiet, a slice of cake was more expensive than expected, and you would return when not in a hurry. Make it sound like a real recommendation rather than a review site entry.

Write 6-8 sentences as a first-person social post about returning to a university library after twelve years. The entrance has moved, the old basement cafe is gone, one reading room looks almost unchanged, and you unexpectedly recognized a librarian who used to work there. Keep the post reflective but resist turning it into nostalgia or a life lesson.

Write 6-8 sentences as a first-person opinion post about paying a little extra for direct flights when traveling with young children. Base it on one trip where a direct flight cost more but avoided a four-hour connection; the outbound flight was delayed 35 minutes anyway; the children slept for part of the flight; and baggage took a long time after arrival. Keep the conclusion qualified rather than universal.

Write 6-8 sentences as a first-person recap of a small neighborhood outdoor concert. It started twenty minutes late, the audience was roughly sixty people, one song had to be restarted because of a microphone problem, children were dancing near the front, and you stayed until the end. Mention whether you would attend again without making the event sound bigger than it was.

Write 6-8 sentences as a first-person recap of a school fundraising evening. There was a short student performance, a used-book table, homemade food sold by parents, and a raffle that ran later than planned. You bought two books and left before the final raffle prize. Keep it personal and concrete; do not praise the 'community spirit' or add a moral.
